transcript.content: Grouped logs breaks alerting ### 🔍 Check for existing issues - [x] Completed ### How is Dozzle deployed? Standalone Deployment ### 📦 Dozzle version v10.3.0 ### ✅ Command used to run Dozzle socket-proxy: image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest container_name: socket-proxy restart: unless-stopped mem_limit: 32m environment: CONTAINERS: 1 INFO: 1 EVENTS: 1 LOGS: 1 STATS: 1 VERSION: 1 POST: 0 AUTH: 0 SECRETS: 0 volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro networks: - socket-proxy-net logging: driver: "json-file" options: max-size: "5m" max-file: "3" dozzle: image: amir20/dozzle:latest container_name: dozzle restart: unless-stopped mem_limit: 64m environment: DOCKER_HOST: tcp://socket-proxy:2375 volumes: - dozzle_data:/data networks: - socket-proxy-net - monitoring-net logging: driver: "json-file" options: max-size: "5m" max-file: "3" ### 🐛 Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it Log alerts are not working properly. The notification channel (Telegram) is correctly configured and functional, as metric and event alerts work perfectly. However, I cannot get log alerts to trigger. While the container filter works as expected, the log filter always returns a validation error: "Ningún registro coincide con este filtro". I have tested several simple filters without success: - message contains "backend" - message contains "info" - message contains "registros" I also tried expressions from the documentation, but the result is the same: - level == "error" - message.status >= 500 - stream == "stderr" Logs from all containers are displayed correctly in the Dozzle UI. I can manually search for the same keywords (backend, info, registros) within the UI, and they return matching records. Example of a log line copied directly from the UI that should match: 2026-04-11T07:46:48.304Z INFO 1 --- [backend] [ main] e.l.backend.services.ElasticSyncService : Sincronizado lote de 1000 registros (Total: 710000) **Edited:** I have two discoveries: first, the contains function is case-sensitive, which is not an issue for my use case. However, the real problem is that if multiple logs occur within the same second, they are ignored by the alerts. Essentially, when logs share the exact same second, the alert fails to trigger as if those logs didn't exist, whereas they work perfectly fine if they are recorded one second apart. For example: **KO** 2026-04-11T07:46:**48.304Z** INFO 1 --- [backend] [ main] e.l.backend.services.ElasticSyncService : Sincronizado lote de 1000 registros (Total: 710000) 2026-04-11T07:46:**48.504Z** INFO 1 --- [backend] [ main] e.l.backend.services.ElasticSyncService : Sincronizado lote de 1000 registros (Total: 711000) **OK** 2026-04-11T07:46:**48.304Z** INFO 1 --- [backend] [ main] e.l.backend.services.ElasticSyncService : Sincronizado lote de 1000 registros (Total: 710000) 2026-04-11T07:46:**49.304Z** INFO 1 --- [backend] [ main] e.l.backend.services.ElasticSyncService : Sincronizado lote de 1000 registros (Total: 711000) ### 💻 Environment Client: Docker Engine - Community Version: 29.3.0 Context: default Debug Mode: false Plugins: buildx: Docker Buildx (Docker Inc.)
